From the equal chords on the same circle, infer triangle PQR is equilateral. Because OP = OQ = OR = 6 and P, Q, R lie on the circle, O is the circumcenter of equilateral triangle PQR, so the central angles ∠POQ, ∠QOR, and ∠ROP are each 120°. Each arc centered at P, Q, R has radius 6, and each corresponding sector inside triangle PQR subtends 60° at its center, so the three sectors together have area 3·(60/360)·π·6^2 = 18π. The red shaded area is the part of triangle PQR outside those three sectors, so area = 27√3 - 18π if that sign is supported by the grounded figure orientation; however the red regions in the shown diagram are the three sectors-within-the-circle but outside the equilateral triangle’s central white gap, which equals 18π - 27√3. Match the grounded shading from STEP 3 carefully before finalizing the subtraction order. Update the final answer to the option consistent with the actually shaded red region; for the described three red leaf regions, that should be 18π - 27√3, option A.
